SearchAliases: not falling under cause and effect
Senses.Explanation: A fox story becomes a named public case: the story's unnamed former abbot says that answering 'does not fall under cause and effect' brought five hundred fox births, while Baizhang Huaihai answers 'is not blind to cause and effect.' Zhenjing Kewen heads a verse simply 'Wild Fox'; Huiji Yuanxi repeatedly raises 'Baizhang's wild-fox story' in the chamber to question Daxin, and Shita Xuanmi raises the same longer title in a hall address. The abbreviated case-name is a textual object, not the animal in the story and not a person denounced as a fox.
Senses.Note: Standalone activation is explicit in Zhenjing Kewen's verse heading 'Wild Fox' (野狐). The longer Baizhang, story, and public-case labels are retained as family evidence and do not by themselves create or deepen the bare sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 野狐野狐不落藏鋒不昧分，要伊從此脫狐身。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jiatai Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), in Zhenjing Kewen's explicitly headed verse series. Zhenjing Kewen uses 'Wild Fox' as the verse heading, then versifies the not-falling/not-being-blind contrast and release from the fox body.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師室中常舉百丈野狐話問僧，對者多不契。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xiaoyin Daxin (笑隱大訢禪師語錄), Daxin's funerary biography. Huiji Yuanxi is the named teacher who repeatedly raises Baizhang's wild-fox story in the chamber and questions Daxin; Daxin is the intended respondent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，舉百丈野狐話，乃曰：不是翻濤手，徒誇跨海鯨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Shita Xuanmi section. Shita Xuanmi raises Baizhang's wild-fox story in a hall address and begins his appraisal.

Senses.Explanation: The ordinary animal remains visible: Baizhang Huaihai leads the assembly behind the mountain, draws out a dead fox, and has it cremated. The story's unnamed former abbot says that he fell into fox births and later escaped the fox body; Fachang Yu asks why one falls into or escapes 'the fox,' Hongfu Ziwen says that understanding the paired formulas still leaves one falling into the fox, and Dahui Zonggao calls the former figure that wild fox from five hundred births ago. These named predicates still denote the animal or animal incarnation, not the name of the case and not an insult directed at a person.
Senses.Note: Baizhang Huaihai supplies the corpse and cremation; Fachang Yu and Hongfu Ziwen supply falling-into and escaping-from predicates; Dahui Zonggao supplies the five-hundred-birth fox. The source presents the former abbot without a personal name, so the entry invents no synthetic master identity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師領眾至山後巖下。以杖挑出一死野狐。乃依法火塟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Baizhang Huaihai section. Baizhang leads the assembly behind the mountain, draws out one dead wild fox with his staff, and has it cremated according to the prescribed procedure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 法昌遇云：敢問諸人：不落因果，為甚麼墮野狐？不昧因果，為甚麼脫野狐？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Ancient Cases of the Chan Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), Baizhang case section. Fachang Yu asks the assembly why not falling into cause and effect means falling into a fox and why not being blind to cause and effect means escaping the fox.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉百丈野狐話，頌曰：不昧不落作麼會，會得依前墮野狐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Orthodox Succession of the Continued Lamp (續燈正統), Hongfu Ziwen section. Hongfu Ziwen raises the named case and says that even understanding not-being-blind and not-falling leaves one falling into the fox as before.

Occurrences.Kwic: 徑山杲云：不落與不昧，半明還半晦；不昧與不落，兩頭空索索。五百生前箇野狐，而今冷地謾追呼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Ancient Cases of the Chan Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), explicitly introducing Jingshan Gao. Dahui Zonggao calls the case's former figure 'that wild fox from five hundred births ago' while versifying the paired formulas.

Senses.PreferredTarget: a person denounced as a wild fox
Senses.Explanation: A person or group is denounced as a wild fox: Zhongan Huikong says he exposes all the wild foxes under heaven, while Deshan Xuanjian coordinates people he rejects with spirits, apparitions, and wild foxes. Nanyang Huizhong's longer 'wild-fox spirit' sharpens the personal insult. Dahui Zonggao applies the still longer fox-spirit label to an understanding, but Dahui's nested compound does not make views a bare-word referent. This abusive human label is not the literal fox body or the title of the Baizhang case, and the entry does not make each named rebuke an objective verdict.
Senses.Note: Zhongan Huikong's 'all the wild foxes under heaven' and Deshan Xuanjian's pairing 'spirits and wild foxes' independently activate the epithet for people and groups. Nanyang Huizhong's 'wild-fox spirit' and Dahui Zonggao's 'wild-fox-spirit understanding' remain family compounds; Dahui's form shows a related view-insult but does not extend the bare sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 等閑拋出東山暗號，驗盡天下野狐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jiatai Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), Zhongan Huikong section. Zhongan Huikong says that casting out Dongshan's secret signal tests all the wild foxes under heaven.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若有一塵一法可得與儞執取生解，保任貴重者，盡落天魔外道。是有學得底，亦是依草附木，精魅野狐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Lamp Record (聯燈會要), Deshan Xuanjian's explicitly headed address. Deshan Xuanjian calls learned, clung-to formulations dependent spirits, apparitions, and wild foxes.

Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in the inherited Nanyang Huizhong–Dazhu Huizang exchange. Nanyang rebukes Dazhu as 'this wild-fox spirit' after Dazhu's third answer about where he dwells.
Orthodox Succession of the Continued Lamp (續燈正統), Dahui Zonggao section. Dahui Zonggao warns that the material at issue must not all be made into a wild-fox-spirit understanding.
